newsitem.title: USA: US late spot prods feel NYMEX sting, diffs stable.
newsitem.headline: US late spot prods feel NYMEX sting, diffs stable.

text.p: U.S. spot product prices were pulled sharply lower by NYMEX futures late Wednesday, players said, although most differentials remained stable in thin trade.
Refined products were caught in a harsh NYMEX downdraft, with May gasoline falling 2.06 cents to 60.61 cents a gallon and heating oil settling 1.43 cents lower to 52.52 cents a gallon.

"The only bullish thing to say, technically, is that the market has fallen too quickly and is 'due for a correction,'" one Gulf player said, citing recent bearish fundamentals such as mild winter weather and oversupply of crude .
Activity in the spot markets picked up slightly from the torpor that marked the previous few days, traders said, but was far from energetic.
"I think we've hit the spring doldrums early this year," one market player said of the modest activity.
U.S. Gulf No. 2 oil diffs firmed slightly, with back 10th cycle barrels on the Colonial Pipeline offered at 1.75 cents under the NYMEX print, up about 0.10 cent on the day.
USG low sulphur diesel, however, remained steady, with players putting 10th cycle barrels between about 0.45 and 0.60 cents over the screen.
